learn.hook: Is your home full of cousins, or is it just you and your parents? Every family is special!
points: A family is a group of people who live together, love each other and look after each other.
A small family may have only parents and their children.
A big joint family may have grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins living together.
Some children live with one parent, or with grandparents. These are loving families too.
We have special names for relatives, like dadi, nani, chacha, mama, bua and mausi.

example.q: Kabir lives with his mother, father, dadi, dadu, chacha, chachi and two cousins. What kind of family is this?
steps: Count who lives in the home: parents, grandparents, an uncle, an aunt and cousins.
Many relatives from different generations live together under one roof.
A family like this is called a joint family.
example.answer: A joint family

learn.reallife: At a family wedding or a festival you may meet many relatives at once. Ask an elder to tell you how each one is related to you!

games.title: Small or joint family?
items: Ammi, Abbu and their two children
Papa, Ma, baby Tara and Dev
A child living with parents only
Parents, children, dadi and dadu, all in one home
Two brothers, their wives and all their children together
Grandparents, uncle, aunt and cousins sharing a home
Three generations living under one roof

quiz.q: Meena lives with her mother, father and little brother. What kind of family is this?
quiz.explain: Parents and their children living together make a small family.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a family must have many members

quiz.q: Who is your mother's brother?
quiz.explain: Your mother's brother is your mama. Your father's younger brother is your chacha.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up mother's side and father's side relatives

quiz.q: Who is your father's mother?
quiz.explain: Your father's mother is your dadi. Your mother's mother is your nani.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up dadi and nani

quiz.q: In a joint family, who usually lives together?
options: Grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and cousins
quiz.explain: A joint family has many relatives from different generations living in one home.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a joint family with a small family

quiz.q: Aman lives with his nani and nana. Is this a real family?
options: Yes, people who live together and care for each other are a family
No, a family must have a mother and father
No, a family must have ten people
Only if they have a big house
quiz.explain: Families come in many shapes. Love and care make a family, not its size.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there is only one correct kind of family

quiz.q: Your bua is your father's ___.
quiz.explain: Bua is the name for your father's sister.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up bua with chacha

quiz.q: Which of these is a good thing about living in a joint family?
options: You never have to help anyone
There are many people to share work and stories with
There is no one to play with
quiz.explain: In a joint family, many hands share the work, and children get to hear stories from grandparents.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a big family means less help and company

quiz.q: Two new babies are born in Pooja's small family of 3. How many people are in her family now?
quiz.explain: There were 3 people. 2 babies joined. 3 + 2 = 5.
steps: Start with 3 people
Add 2 babies: 3 + 2 = 5
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the new members

teach.ask: Gappu lives only with his mama bird. He asks: is that a real family? What is a family?
teach.praise: Tweet! So my nest is a real family too. Thank you!
teach.nudge: But do all families have the same number of people?

learn.hook: Dadi's stories are the best! But who helps Dadi when her knees hurt?
points: Elders are older people like grandparents. They have lots of love and lots of stories.
As people grow old, they may walk slowly, see less clearly or forget things.
We can help them: fetch their glasses, read to them, or walk slowly beside them.
Spending time and talking with elders makes them happy.
We show respect by speaking politely and listening to them.

example.q: Nanu's glasses are in the next room and he wants to read the newspaper. What can Asha do?
steps: Think: Nanu needs glasses to read, and walking is hard for him.
Asha can bring the glasses to him.
She can also offer to read the news aloud with him.
example.answer: Bring Nanu his glasses, or read the newspaper aloud to him

learn.reallife: When your grandparents visit or call, tell them about your school day. They love hearing from you!

games.title: Kind or not?
items: Walking slowly with Dadi so she does not have to hurry is kind.
Matching her speed keeps her safe and comfortable.
Laughing when Nanu forgets a name is a good way to help.
Laughing can hurt his feelings. We can gently remind him instead.
Reading a story aloud to a grandparent is a way to spend time together.
Reading together is fun and helps elders who find small print hard to see.
Elders can teach us games, songs and recipes.
Elders know many old games, songs and family recipes.
Respect means speaking politely and calmly.
Helping Dadu remember his medicine time is a caring thing to do.
Elders may forget, so a gentle reminder helps them stay healthy.

items.text: Bring Nani her ___ so she can read.
Walk ___ with Dadu when you go to the park.
Speak ___ to all elders.
Sit and ___ to Dadi's stories.

quiz.q: Dadi finds it hard to climb stairs. How can you help?
options: Hold her hand and go up slowly with her
Run up and leave her behind
quiz.explain: Walking slowly beside her and giving a hand keeps her safe.
quiz.mistake: Thinks hurrying elders is helpful

quiz.q: Nana wants to talk about his childhood. What should Ravi do?
quiz.explain: Listening shows love and respect. Elders' stories also teach us about the past.
quiz.mistake: Does not see listening as a way of caring

quiz.q: Why might elders need help with small things?
options: Elders do not like to do anything
As people grow old, their bodies can become weaker
quiz.explain: Old age can make eyes, knees and memory weaker, so small tasks may become hard.
quiz.mistake: Blames elders instead of understanding old age

quiz.q: Which of these shows respect for elders?
quiz.explain: Greeting elders politely, like saying namaste, shows respect.
quiz.mistake: Confuses rude actions with respectful ones

quiz.q: Nani often forgets to drink water. What is a caring idea?
options: Remind her gently and bring her a glass of water
quiz.explain: A gentle reminder helps her stay healthy without hurting her feelings.
quiz.mistake: Thinks scolding is the same as helping

quiz.q: What can grandparents teach us?
options: Old stories, songs and family recipes
quiz.explain: Elders have lived a long life and know many stories, songs and recipes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks elders have nothing to share

quiz.q: Dadu lives in another city. How can Sana stay close to him?
options: Call him and tell him about her day
quiz.explain: Phone calls, letters and visits keep us close to elders who live far away.
quiz.mistake: Thinks caring is only possible when living together

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a kind way to help an elder?
options: Helping them cross a road with an adult
Taking away their walking stick for fun
quiz.explain: A walking stick helps elders balance. Taking it away could make them fall.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the elder's safety

teach.ask: Gappu's grandpa bird is getting old and slow. Gappu asks: how can I take care of him?
teach.praise: Chirp! I will help Grandpa and listen to his stories every day!
teach.nudge: How should I talk to Grandpa so he feels respected?

learn.hook: What makes a friend a good friend? Is it sharing laddoos? Maybe!
points: Friends play together, share things and help each other.
Good friends take turns, say sorry when they make a mistake and forgive each other.
Friends can be different from us. They may speak another language or like other games.
Including a new child in your game is a kind thing to do.
Friends cheer for each other and feel happy for each other.

example.q: A new girl, Lhamo, has joined your class from Sikkim. She sits alone at lunch. What can you do?
steps: Think: being new can feel lonely.
You can smile, say hello and ask her name.
Invite her to sit with your group and play at break.
example.answer: Say hello, ask her name and invite her to join you

learn.reallife: At school, in the park or in your colony, a kind word can start a new friendship.

games.title: Friendship facts
items: Taking turns is fair, so everyone gets a chance.
A friend must speak the same language as you.
Friends can speak different languages and learn from each other.
Saying sorry after a mistake helps a friendship.
It shows you care about your friend's feelings.
Leaving a new child out of every game is kind.
Inviting a new child to play is the kind thing to do.
Friends feel happy when the other one does well.
Good friends cheer for each other.

quiz.q: Arjun and Imran both want the swing. What should they do?
quiz.explain: Taking turns is fair. Both friends get to enjoy the swing.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the strongest child should get it

quiz.q: You broke your friend's pencil by mistake. What should you say?
quiz.explain: Saying sorry shows you care about your friend's feelings.
quiz.mistake: Thinks hiding a mistake is better than owning it

quiz.q: Which of these is a good friend?
options: Someone who teases you all the time
Someone who helps you when you are sad
Someone who tells lies about you
quiz.explain: A good friend is kind and helps you when you need it.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what makes someone a good friend

quiz.q: A new boy who speaks Tamil joins your class. You speak Hindi. Can you be friends?
options: No, friends must speak the same language
Yes, friends can speak different languages
quiz.explain: Friendship is about kindness. You can even teach each other words in your languages!
quiz.mistake: Thinks friends must be the same as us

quiz.q: Your friend wins the drawing contest. What is a friendly thing to do?
options: Say it was a bad drawing
quiz.explain: Good friends are happy for each other's success.
quiz.mistake: Feels jealous instead of happy

quiz.q: Your friend forgot his tiffin. What can you do?
options: Eat in front of him and laugh
Share some of your food with him
quiz.explain: Sharing food when a friend has none is a caring thing to do.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how the friend feels

quiz.q: Your friend shares a secret about a surprise party. What should you do?
options: Keep the surprise until the party
quiz.explain: Friends trust each other. Keeping a happy surprise secret shows you are trustworthy.
quiz.mistake: Does not value trust in friendship

quiz.q: Riya has 6 toffees. She shares them equally with her friend Neha. How many toffees does each girl get?
quiz.explain: 6 toffees shared equally between 2 girls is 3 each.
steps: 2 girls share 6 toffees
6 ÷ 2 = 3 each
quiz.mistake: Gives all toffees to one person instead of sharing equally

teach.ask: Gappu wants a new friend at the bird school. He asks: how can I be a good friend?
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! I will share my seeds and take turns on the branch!
teach.nudge: What should I say if I hurt my friend by mistake?

learn.hook: Giant wheels, jalebis and balloons everywhere! Shall we go to the mela?
points: A mela is a big fair where many people come together to shop, eat and have fun.
At a mela you see rides like the giant wheel and the merry-go-round.
There are stalls selling bangles, toys, pots, clothes and tasty snacks.
Many melas are held at festival times or after the harvest.
Some melas are famous, like the Pushkar fair in Rajasthan, where camels are brought for trade.

example.q: Tara has ₹50. A balloon costs ₹10 and a plate of jalebi costs ₹30. If she buys both, how much money is left?
steps: Add the costs: ₹10 + ₹30 = ₹40.
Take it away from what she has: ₹50 − ₹40 = ₹10.
Planning before spending helps us buy what we really want.

learn.reallife: Melas are held in many towns and villages. Look out for one near you at festival time, and always go with a grown-up.

items.text: The big round ride that goes up high is the giant ___.
The Pushkar fair is famous for its ___.
Colourful glass ___ are sold at a bangle stall.
Many melas are held after the ___ of crops.

quiz.q: What is a mela?
options: A big fair where people shop, eat and enjoy rides
quiz.explain: A mela is a fair. People gather there to shop, eat, watch shows and enjoy rides.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word mela

quiz.q: Which of these would you most likely ride at a mela?
quiz.explain: Merry-go-rounds and giant wheels are common mela rides.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up fair rides with real travel

quiz.q: The Pushkar fair is held in which state?
quiz.explain: The Pushkar fair is held in Pushkar, a town in Rajasthan.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a state without knowing the fair

quiz.q: Which animal is the Pushkar fair famous for?
quiz.explain: Many camels are brought to the Pushkar fair to be decorated, shown and traded.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the desert state with camels

quiz.q: Why do many melas happen after harvest time?
options: Farmers have finished their work and have crops to sell and celebrate
Shops in the city are closed
quiz.explain: After the harvest, farmers have time and something to celebrate, so many melas happen then.
quiz.mistake: Does not link melas with farming life

quiz.q: Ravi has ₹40. A toy costs ₹25. How much money will he have left?
steps: He has ₹40
He spends ₹25
quiz.mistake: Adds the money instead of taking away

quiz.q: At a mela, a person makes puppets dance with strings. What is this show called?
quiz.explain: Puppets moved by strings, called kathputli, are a famous folk art of Rajasthan.
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise a puppet show

quiz.q: Which of these is a snack you might find at a mela?
quiz.explain: Jalebi is a sweet snack fried fresh at many melas.
quiz.mistake: Picks an item that is not food

teach.ask: Gappu has never been to a mela. He asks: what happens at a mela?
teach.praise: Chirp! I want to ride the giant wheel and eat jalebi!
teach.nudge: What can I buy or eat at a mela?

learn.hook: Who blows up all those balloons? Who makes the bangles? Let's meet the mela workers!
points: Many people work hard to make a mela fun for us.
A potter makes pots and diyas from clay.
A balloon seller, a toy seller and a bangle seller sell their goods at stalls.
Cooks fry snacks, and ride operators run the giant wheel safely.
Every kind of work is useful, and we should respect every worker.

example.q: At the mela, Gopal sells clay pots and diyas that he made on a spinning wheel. What is his work called?
steps: Think: he makes things from clay.
He shapes them on a spinning wheel.
A person who makes things from clay is a potter.
example.answer: He is a potter

learn.reallife: In your neighbourhood you can see many workers too: the vegetable seller, the cobbler, the tailor and the sweeper. Thank them!

quiz.q: Who makes clay pots and diyas?
quiz.explain: A potter shapes wet clay, often on a spinning wheel, and then bakes it to make it hard.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up different kinds of workers

quiz.q: Why should we respect every worker at the mela?
options: Every kind of work is useful and needs effort
quiz.explain: From the sweeper to the cook, every worker helps the mela run well.
quiz.mistake: Thinks some honest work is less important

quiz.q: Who runs the giant wheel?
quiz.explain: A ride operator starts, stops and looks after the ride so people stay safe.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about who runs the rides

quiz.q: A woman draws pretty patterns on people's hands with henna. She is a ___.
quiz.explain: Mehendi artists draw designs with henna paste, which leaves an orange-brown colour.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up mehendi with other crafts

quiz.q: After the mela ends, who cleans up the ground?
quiz.explain: Cleaners pick up litter so the ground is clean again. We can help by using dustbins.
quiz.mistake: Thinks places clean themselves

quiz.q: Which of these is the best way to treat a stall owner?
options: Speak politely and say thank you
quiz.explain: Being polite and paying for what we take shows respect for their work.
quiz.mistake: Does not see sellers as people doing work

quiz.q: A man makes a show where puppets dance on strings. Which state is this kathputli art famous in?
quiz.explain: Kathputli string puppets are a famous folk art of Rajasthan.
quiz.mistake: Guesses without knowing the art form

quiz.q: Which worker would you need to fix a torn chappal at the mela?
quiz.explain: A cobbler repairs shoes and chappals.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up cobbler with other workers

teach.ask: Gappu saw so many people at the mela. He asks: who are they and what do they do?
teach.praise: Tweet! Everyone works so hard. I will say thank you to them all!
teach.nudge: Should I respect all the workers, or only some of them?

learn.hook: A mela is fun but very crowded. What if you lose your family? Here's how to stay safe!
points: Always stay close to your grown-up and hold their hand in a crowd.
Learn your full name, your parent's name and phone number by heart.
Fix a meeting place, like the big gate, in case you get separated.
If you are lost, stay where you are or go to a help desk or a police officer.
Never go anywhere with a stranger, even if they offer sweets or toys.

example.q: Mohan cannot find his mother at the mela. What should he do?
steps: First, do not panic and do not wander far away.
Look for the help desk, a police officer or a stall owner near the meeting place.
Tell them his name and his mother's name and phone number.
example.answer: Stay calm, go to the help desk or a police officer, and share his parent's name and phone number

learn.reallife: In India, 112 is the emergency number. A grown-up can call it for help anywhere.

games.title: Safe or not safe?
items: Holding a grown-up's hand in a crowd is safe.
It is hard to get lost when you hold hands.
Going with a stranger who offers toffees is safe.
Never go with a stranger. Tell a trusted adult.
Knowing your parent's phone number by heart helps if you get lost.
Helpers can call your parent right away.
Pushing people in a crowd is a good way to move faster.
Pushing can make people fall and get hurt.
A police officer or help desk can help a lost child.
They are there to help people at the mela.
If you are lost, you should run around everywhere to search.
Running around makes it harder to find you. Stay near a safe place or a help desk.

games.title: If you get lost
games.prompt: Put the safe steps in order
items: Look for the help desk or a police officer
Tell them your name and your parent's phone number
Wait there until your family comes

quiz.q: What should you do in a big crowd at the mela?
quiz.explain: Holding hands keeps you close to your family in a crowd.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is fine to wander alone

quiz.q: A stranger says, 'Come with me, I will buy you a toy.' What should you do?
options: Say no and go to your grown-up
quiz.explain: Never go with a stranger. Say no and tell a trusted adult at once.
quiz.mistake: Trusts a stranger because of a treat

quiz.q: Which information should you know by heart?
options: Your name and your parent's phone number
quiz.explain: If you are lost, helpers can contact your family with your parent's name and phone number.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why the phone number matters

quiz.q: Who is a safe person to ask for help if you are lost at a mela?
options: A police officer or the help desk
quiz.explain: Police officers and help desk staff are there to help lost children.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any friendly stranger is safe

quiz.q: What is the emergency helpline number in India that works across the country?
quiz.explain: 112 is India's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance help.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with numbers from films or other countries

quiz.q: Why should a family fix a meeting place before entering the mela?
options: So they can leave the children there
So everyone knows where to go if they get separated
quiz.explain: A meeting place like the main gate helps a lost person find the family quickly.
quiz.mistake: Does not plan ahead for getting lost

quiz.q: Why should we not push in a crowd?
options: People may fall and get hurt
quiz.explain: Pushing can make people fall. Walking calmly keeps everyone safe.
quiz.mistake: Thinks pushing saves time

quiz.q: You are lost and scared. What is the FIRST thing to do?
options: Go out of the mela gate alone
quiz.explain: Staying calm helps you think and find a helper. Running away makes it harder for your family to find you.
quiz.mistake: Panics instead of staying in one safe place

teach.ask: Gappu is going to a very crowded bird mela. He asks: how do I stay safe there?
teach.praise: Chirp! I will stay close to Mama and remember our phone number!
teach.nudge: What should I do if I get lost?

learn.hook: India has so many festivals that there is something to celebrate almost every month!
points: People of many religions and regions live in India, so we have many festivals.
Diwali is the festival of lights, and Holi is the festival of colours.
Eid ul-Fitr comes at the end of the month of Ramzan. Christmas is celebrated on 25 December.
Harvest festivals thank nature for crops: Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Bihu in Assam, Baisakhi in Punjab and Onam in Kerala.
National festivals belong to every Indian: Republic Day on 26 January, Independence Day on 15 August and Gandhi Jayanti on 2 October.

example.q: Farmers in Tamil Nadu cook rice with milk and jaggery in a new pot to thank the Sun and the cattle for a good crop. Which festival is this?
steps: The clues are: Tamil Nadu, new rice, and thanking nature for a crop.
That makes it a harvest festival of Tamil Nadu.
The festival, and the sweet rice dish too, is called Pongal.
example.answer: Pongal

learn.reallife: Look at a calendar at home. Circle the festivals your family celebrates and the ones your friends celebrate!

quiz.q: Which festival is called the festival of lights?
quiz.explain: On Diwali, people light diyas and lamps in and around their homes.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Diwali and Holi

quiz.q: Which festival is known as the festival of colours?
quiz.explain: On Holi, people play with colours and coloured water.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Holi with other festivals

quiz.q: On which date do we celebrate Christmas?
quiz.explain: Christmas is celebrated every year on 25 December.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Christmas with a national festival date

quiz.q: Onam is a harvest festival of which state?
quiz.explain: Onam is Kerala's harvest festival, with flower pookalams and a big feast.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up harvest festivals of different states

quiz.q: Bihu is a festival of which state?
quiz.explain: Bihu is celebrated in Assam with music and the lively Bihu dance.
quiz.mistake: Thinks Bihu belongs to Bihar because the names sound alike

quiz.q: Which of these is a national festival celebrated by all Indians?
quiz.explain: Independence Day, on 15 August, is celebrated all over India by everyone.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a regional festival with a national festival

quiz.q: Eid ul-Fitr is celebrated at the end of which month?
quiz.explain: Eid ul-Fitr comes at the end of Ramzan, the month of fasting.
quiz.mistake: Does not know when Eid ul-Fitr comes

quiz.q: Why are Pongal, Bihu and Baisakhi called harvest festivals?
options: They happen in the rainy night
They are celebrated when crops are ready and gathered
quiz.explain: These festivals celebrate the crops being gathered and thank nature for food.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what harvest means

teach.ask: Gappu sees lights one month and colours the next. He asks: why does India have so many festivals?
teach.praise: Tweet! India is like a big garden of festivals!
teach.nudge: Are there festivals for the crops too?

learn.hook: Every festival has a special smell — sweets frying, flowers, fresh paint. Let's explore festival customs!
points: Each festival has special foods. Modaks for Ganesh Chaturthi, sevaiyan for Eid and cake for Christmas.
On Makar Sankranti, people fly kites and eat sweets made of til (sesame) and gur (jaggery).
In Kerala, the Onam feast, called sadya, is served on a banana leaf.
People decorate homes with rangoli, kolam, lights or flowers, and often wear new clothes.
At a gurdwara, people of every background sit together and eat free food at the langar.

example.q: Fatima's family is making sweet vermicelli cooked in milk and greeting neighbours with 'Eid Mubarak'. Which dish is this?
steps: Vermicelli is thin noodle-like strands.
Sweet vermicelli in milk is a favourite festival dish for Eid.
It is called sevaiyan (or sheer khurma).
example.answer: Sevaiyan

learn.reallife: Ask your family which special dish they make for a festival, and help them make it with an adult watching.

items.text: People fly ___ on Makar Sankranti.
Diyas are lit on ___.
Pookalam is made with ___ during Onam.
Free community food at a gurdwara is called ___.
People decorate a tree with stars and lights for ___.

quiz.q: Which sweet is offered during Ganesh Chaturthi?
quiz.explain: Modak, a sweet dumpling with coconut and jaggery, is linked with Ganesh Chaturthi.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up festival foods

quiz.q: What do people fly on Makar Sankranti?
quiz.explain: Flying kites is a big Makar Sankranti custom, especially in Gujarat and Rajasthan.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the kite custom

quiz.q: Til-gur sweets are made from sesame and ___.
quiz.explain: Til means sesame and gur means jaggery. They are mixed to make sweets for Makar Sankranti.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what gur means

quiz.q: On what is the Onam sadya served?
quiz.explain: The Onam feast is served on a banana leaf, a custom from Kerala.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the sadya custom

quiz.q: What is a langar?
options: Free food served to everyone at a gurdwara
quiz.explain: At the langar, everyone sits together and eats the same food, no matter who they are.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up langar with other customs

quiz.q: Colourful patterns drawn at the doorstep with rice flour or coloured powder are called ___.
quiz.explain: Rangoli and kolam are floor patterns that welcome guests during festivals.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rangoli with mehendi on hands

quiz.q: Which item is used to decorate homes at Christmas?
options: A decorated Christmas tree with a star
quiz.explain: Families decorate a Christmas tree with lights, bells and a star on top.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up decorations of different festivals

quiz.q: Gujiya is a sweet many families make for which festival?
quiz.explain: Gujiya, a sweet stuffed pastry, is popular at Holi in north India.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up festival sweets

teach.ask: Gappu wants to join the festival fun. He asks: what special things do people do on festivals?
teach.praise: Chirp! I will make a tiny rangoli with seeds!
teach.nudge: What special food do people make for festivals?

learn.hook: A festival is more fun with friends! Why do we love celebrating together?
points: Festivals bring families, friends and neighbours together.
People share sweets and greet each other, like 'Happy Diwali' or 'Eid Mubarak'.
Many of us join friends in celebrating their festivals too.
We can celebrate kindly: use natural colours on Holi and keep noise low so pets, birds and elders are not scared.
On national festivals, all of us celebrate together as Indians.

example.q: Neha's neighbour Joseph invites her family for Christmas. Neha's family invites Joseph's family for Diwali. What does this show?
steps: Both families share each other's happy days.
They learn about each other's customs.
This shows friendship and togetherness among neighbours.
example.answer: Festivals help neighbours share joy and come closer

learn.reallife: Your school may celebrate many festivals together in the assembly. Each one is a chance to learn something new.

games.title: Celebrating together
items: We can greet a friend on their festival even if our family does not celebrate it.
Wishing friends on their festival is kind and friendly.
Loud crackers can scare dogs, cats and birds.
Animals have sharp hearing, so loud bangs frighten them.
Throwing colour on someone who says no is good fun.
We should play only with those who want to play.
Republic Day is celebrated by all Indians.
It is a national festival for every Indian.
Sharing sweets with neighbours is a common festival custom.
Many families share sweets with neighbours and friends.
Festivals are only for people of one region.
Many festivals are enjoyed by people from all over India.

games.title: Kind or unkind festival habit?
items: Inviting a new friend to join
Helping clean up after a party
Throwing colour on people who say no

quiz.q: Why do people say festivals bring us together?
options: Families, friends and neighbours celebrate and share joy
quiz.explain: Festivals are times to meet, share food and enjoy together.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the social side of festivals

quiz.q: Your friend Harpreet celebrates Gurpurab. What is a friendly thing to do?
options: Tell her it is not a real festival
quiz.explain: Wishing friends on their festivals shows respect and friendship.
quiz.mistake: Does not respect other people's festivals

quiz.q: Why should we avoid very loud crackers?
options: They scare animals and disturb babies and elders
quiz.explain: Loud bangs frighten animals and can trouble babies, elders and sick people. Smoke also dirties the air.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about others who are affected

quiz.q: Which is a nature-friendly way to play Holi?
options: Use paint from the shop wall
Use colours made from flowers and turmeric
quiz.explain: Natural colours from flowers, leaves and turmeric are gentler on skin and nature.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any colour is safe to use

quiz.q: On Independence Day, schools hoist the national flag. Who celebrates this day?
quiz.explain: Independence Day is a national festival for every Indian, everywhere.
quiz.mistake: Thinks national festivals belong to only some people

quiz.q: What do people often say to each other on Eid?
quiz.explain: 'Eid Mubarak' means 'blessed Eid'. People hug and greet each other with these words.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up festival greetings

quiz.q: After the colony Diwali party, the park is full of wrappers. What should the children do?
options: Help clean up and put waste in dustbins
Hide the wrappers under the swings
quiz.explain: Celebrating together also means cleaning up together.
quiz.mistake: Thinks someone else will always clean up

quiz.q: Which of these shows togetherness during a festival?
options: Eating alone and hiding the sweets
quiz.explain: Sharing food with neighbours brings people closer.
quiz.mistake: Confuses selfish actions with celebration

teach.ask: Gappu's neighbours are celebrating a festival he does not know. He asks: can I join them? Why do festivals matter?
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! I will wish my neighbours and share my seeds!
teach.nudge: What can I share with my neighbours on a festival?

learn.hook: A plant is like a little factory with many parts. Each part has its own job!
points: Most plants have roots, a stem, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds.
Roots grow under the soil. They hold the plant firmly and take in water from the soil.
The stem holds the plant up and carries water from the roots to the leaves.
Leaves make food for the plant using sunlight, air and water.
Plants come in many sizes: tiny grass, bushy shrubs like the rose, and tall trees like the neem and banyan.

example.q: Anu pulls a weed out of the garden. It comes out with long thin threads at the bottom, full of soil. What are these threads, and what did they do for the weed?
steps: The threads were under the soil.
The part of a plant that grows under the soil is the root.
Roots hold the plant in the soil and take in water.
example.answer: They are roots. They held the weed in the soil and took in water.

learn.reallife: Next time you water a pot plant, remember: the roots drink the water, and the stem carries it up to the leaves.

games.title: Part and its job
pairs: Holds the plant in the soil
Carries water up to the leaves
Can grow into a new plant

games.title: A tree from bottom to top
games.prompt: Start from the part deep in the soil

quiz.q: Which part of a plant holds it firmly in the soil?
quiz.explain: Roots spread in the soil and hold the plant in place, like an anchor.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the stem holds the plant in the soil

quiz.q: Which part carries water from the roots to the leaves?
quiz.explain: The stem works like a pipe that carries water up to the leaves.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the jobs of roots and stems

quiz.q: Which part of a plant makes food for it?
quiz.explain: Leaves use sunlight, air and water to make food for the plant.
quiz.mistake: Thinks plants take food from the soil

quiz.q: A carrot is which part of the plant?
quiz.explain: The orange part of a carrot grows under the soil. It is a root that stores food.
quiz.mistake: Thinks everything we eat is a fruit

quiz.q: Which of these is a tall tree?
quiz.explain: Neem grows into a big tree with a thick, hard trunk. The others are small plants.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up herbs with trees

quiz.q: Which plant is a shrub — bushy, with many woody stems, but not as tall as a tree?
quiz.explain: A rose plant is a shrub. Mango, peepal and coconut are tall trees.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any plant with flowers is a tree

quiz.q: The thick, hard stem of a tree is called the ___.
quiz.explain: A tree's main stem is called its trunk. It is hard and woody.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word trunk

quiz.q: Most plants need which of these to grow well?
quiz.explain: Plants need sunlight, water and air to make food and stay healthy.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what plants need

teach.ask: Gappu sees a plant in a pot and wonders what all its parts do. Can you explain?
teach.praise: Chirp! Roots drink, the stem carries and the leaves cook. What a team!
teach.nudge: Which part makes food for the plant?

learn.hook: Have you ever seen two leaves that look exactly alike? Leaves and flowers are full of surprises!
points: Leaves come in many shapes and sizes: the banana leaf is huge, and the tulsi leaf is small.
A leaf has a flat part, thin lines called veins, and a small stalk joining it to the stem.
Most leaves are green. Leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant.
Flowers have colourful petals and many have a sweet smell.
Bees and butterflies visit flowers. After this, many flowers grow into fruits with seeds inside.

example.q: Rohit sees bees buzzing around the mustard flowers in the field. Later, the flowers turn into thin pods. What is happening?
steps: Bees visit flowers to drink their sweet juice, called nectar.
This visit helps the flowers to make seeds.
The flowers then change into pods, which are the fruits that hold mustard seeds.
example.answer: The flowers are turning into pods (fruits) with seeds inside

learn.reallife: Collect fallen leaves in your park and compare their shapes, sizes and edges. Do not pluck leaves from plants!

games.title: Leaf and flower facts
items: A banana leaf is bigger than a tulsi leaf.
Banana leaves are big enough to eat a meal on!
Leaves have thin lines on them called veins.
Veins carry water through the leaf.
Leaves make food for the plant using sunlight.
That is why most plants grow towards light.
Flowers come in many colours, like yellow marigolds and white jasmine.
Bees visit flowers for their sweet nectar.
Bees use nectar to make honey.
The lotus grows in ponds and lakes.

quiz.q: Which part do we eat in spinach (palak)?
quiz.explain: We cook and eat the green leaves of the spinach plant.
quiz.mistake: Does not link vegetables to plant parts

quiz.q: Which part of the cauliflower plant do we eat?
quiz.explain: The white part of a cauliflower is a tight bunch of flower buds.
quiz.mistake: Thinks cauliflower is a leaf because it is a vegetable

quiz.q: The thin lines you see on a leaf are called ___.
quiz.explain: Veins are thin lines that carry water to all parts of the leaf.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up leaf parts with flower parts

quiz.q: Why do bees visit flowers?
options: To build nests in the stem
quiz.explain: Bees drink nectar from flowers and use it to make honey.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what bees get from flowers

quiz.q: Which flower grows in ponds and is India's national flower?
quiz.explain: The lotus grows in water and is the national flower of India.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a popular garden flower

quiz.q: Which of these is the colourful part of a flower?
quiz.explain: Petals are the soft, colourful parts of a flower.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up flower parts with tree parts

quiz.q: Which plant has very big leaves that are used as plates in South India?
quiz.explain: Banana leaves are large and strong, so food is served on them.
quiz.mistake: Picks a plant with small leaves

quiz.q: After a flower is visited by bees, what does it often grow into?
quiz.explain: Many flowers turn into fruits, and the fruits hold seeds.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that fruits come from flowers

teach.ask: Gappu found a fallen leaf and a flower. He asks: what is special about leaves and flowers?
teach.praise: Tweet! Leaves cook food and flowers turn into fruits. Wow!
teach.nudge: What do flowers grow into?

learn.hook: A giant banyan tree starts as one tiny seed. How does a seed become a plant?
points: Seeds are found inside fruits. A mango has one big seed; a papaya has many small seeds.
A seed can grow into a new plant when it gets water, air and warmth.
When a seed starts to grow, a tiny root comes out first, and then a small shoot.
Seeds travel to new places. Cotton and aak (madar) seeds fly with the wind, coconuts float on water, and birds drop seeds of fruits they eat.
We eat many seeds, like rice, wheat, dal, peas and peanuts.

example.q: Simran soaks moong seeds in water overnight and keeps them wrapped in a wet cloth. After a day, tiny white tails appear. What has happened?
steps: The seeds got water, air and warmth.
They started to grow, which we call sprouting.
The tiny white tail is the first root of the new plant.
example.answer: The seeds have sprouted. The white tail is the first root.

learn.reallife: Sprouted moong is eaten as a healthy snack in many Indian homes. You can grow your own with an adult's help!

games.title: How a seed grows
items: Seed soaks up water and swells

quiz.q: What does a seed need to start growing?
options: A dark plastic box with no air
quiz.explain: Seeds need water, air and warmth to sprout.
quiz.mistake: Thinks seeds can grow without water and air

quiz.q: When a seed sprouts, which part usually comes out first?
quiz.explain: The root comes out first so the young plant can hold on and take in water.
quiz.mistake: Thinks leaves come first

quiz.q: How do cotton seeds travel to new places?
options: They are blown by the wind
quiz.explain: Cotton seeds have soft fluffy hairs that help the wind carry them.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how light seeds spread

quiz.q: How can a coconut travel far away?
quiz.explain: A coconut has a light, hairy covering that helps it float on sea water.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up seed travel methods

quiz.q: Which fruit has only ONE big seed?
quiz.explain: A mango has one big seed in the middle. The others have many seeds.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about seeds inside fruits

quiz.q: Which of these is a seed that we eat?
quiz.explain: Rice grains are seeds. We also eat wheat, dal and peas, which are seeds.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that grains are seeds

quiz.q: Rahul planted 4 seeds in each of his 3 pots. How many seeds did he plant in all?
quiz.explain: 3 pots with 4 seeds in each is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 seeds.
steps: 3 pots × 4 seeds
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers instead of making equal groups

quiz.q: Why do seeds need to travel away from the parent plant?
options: So they can go to school
Because they dislike the parent plant
So they can turn into stones
So the new plants get enough space, water and light
quiz.explain: If all seeds fell under the parent plant, they would be crowded and get less light and water.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why spreading out helps plants

teach.ask: Gappu found a seed and wants it to grow into a tree. He asks: what does a seed need, and how does it grow?
teach.praise: Chirp! I will give my seed water and air and wait for it to sprout!
teach.nudge: What comes out first when a seed starts to grow?

learn.hook: What would a cow, a parrot and a squirrel do without plants? They would be hungry and homeless!
points: Many animals eat plants. Cows and goats eat grass and leaves; parrots eat fruits and seeds.
Bees and butterflies drink nectar from flowers.
Plants give animals shelter. Birds build nests in trees, and squirrels live in tree holes.
Even a tiger needs plants! It eats deer, and deer eat grass and leaves.
We humans also get food, wood and cloth (cotton) from plants.

example.q: A tiger never eats grass. Does it still depend on plants?
steps: A tiger eats animals like deer.
Deer eat grass and leaves to live.
Without plants there would be no deer, so the tiger would have no food.
example.answer: Yes. The tiger eats deer, and deer depend on plants for food.

learn.reallife: Look at the trees near your home. Can you spot a nest, a squirrel or ants climbing up the trunk?

games.title: Who gets what from plants?
pairs: Twigs and grass for a nest
A home in a tree hole

games.title: A food chain
games.prompt: Who is eaten by whom? Start with the plant.

quiz.q: What does a cow eat?
quiz.explain: A cow is a plant-eater. It eats grass, leaves and fodder.
quiz.mistake: Does not know cows eat plants

quiz.q: Where do many birds build their nests?
quiz.explain: Trees give birds a safe, high place to build nests.
quiz.mistake: Does not link birds with trees for shelter

quiz.q: What do bees drink from flowers?
quiz.explain: Nectar is a sweet juice in flowers. Bees use it to make honey.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what nectar is

quiz.q: Lions in the Gir forest of Gujarat eat deer. Deer eat grass. If all the grass dried up, what would happen to the lions?
options: They would have less food, because the deer would go hungry too
quiz.explain: Lions depend on plants through the animals they eat. Less grass means fewer deer for the lions.
quiz.mistake: Thinks meat-eaters do not depend on plants

quiz.q: Which animal eats mainly plants?
quiz.explain: Goats eat grass, leaves and plant parts. The others eat other animals.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up plant-eaters and meat-eaters

quiz.q: Which of these do people get from plants?
quiz.explain: Cotton comes from the cotton plant. Glass, iron and plastic do not come from plants.
quiz.mistake: Does not know cotton comes from a plant

quiz.q: Monkeys live in trees. What else do trees give them?
quiz.explain: Monkeys eat fruits, leaves and flowers from trees.
quiz.mistake: Thinks trees give only shelter

quiz.q: In the food chain 'grass → rabbit → fox', which one makes its own food?
quiz.explain: Plants like grass make their own food using sunlight. Animals cannot make their own food.
quiz.mistake: Thinks animals can make their own food

teach.ask: Gappu wonders why the forest animals need trees and plants. Can you explain?
teach.praise: Chirp! Plants are like a kitchen and a house for animals!
teach.nudge: Do plants give animals a home too?

learn.hook: Plants help animals, but did you know animals help plants too? It is a two-way friendship!
points: When bees and butterflies visit flowers, they carry a yellow powder called pollen from flower to flower. This helps flowers make fruits and seeds.
Birds and animals eat fruits and drop the seeds far away, where new plants can grow.
Some seeds have tiny hooks that stick to animal fur and travel with them.
Earthworms dig in the soil and make it soft and airy, which helps roots grow.
Cow dung is used as manure that makes the soil rich for plants.

example.q: A farmer in Himachal keeps bee boxes in his apple orchard. Why might he do this?
steps: Bees visit apple flowers for nectar.
While doing this, they carry pollen between flowers.
This helps the flowers turn into apples, so the farmer gets more fruit.
example.answer: The bees help the apple flowers make fruit

learn.reallife: Earthworms in your garden soil are tiny helpers. Never harm them — they keep the soil healthy!

games.title: Helping each other
items: Bees carry pollen from one flower to another.
Pollen sticks to their hairy bodies as they move between flowers.
Earthworms make the soil hard and dry.
Earthworms make soil soft and airy.
Birds can help spread seeds to new places.
They eat fruits and drop the seeds far away.
Cow dung can be used as manure for plants.
Dung adds goodness to the soil.
Only plants help animals; animals never help plants.
Animals help plants by spreading pollen and seeds and by improving the soil.

games.title: Who gets help?
items: Bird drops guava seeds far away
Tree gives a bird a place for its nest
Flower gives nectar to a butterfly
Mango tree gives shade to a dog

quiz.q: What do bees carry from one flower to another?
quiz.explain: Pollen is a fine yellow powder. Carrying it between flowers helps them make seeds.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what pollen is

quiz.q: How do birds help plants?
options: They drop seeds in new places
They pour salt on the soil
quiz.explain: Birds eat fruits and later drop the seeds far from the parent tree.
quiz.mistake: Thinks birds only harm plants

quiz.q: How do earthworms help plants?
options: They make the soil soft and airy
They make the leaves fall off
quiz.explain: Earthworms tunnel through soil, letting air and water reach the roots.
quiz.mistake: Thinks earthworms are pests

quiz.q: Why do farmers use cow dung manure in their fields?
options: It keeps the soil dry and empty
It makes the soil rich for plants
quiz.explain: Manure adds nutrients to the soil, so crops grow well.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what manure does

quiz.q: Seeds with tiny hooks travel by ___.
options: Sticking to animal fur and clothes
quiz.explain: Hooks help seeds hold on to fur or clothes, so animals carry them to new places.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up ways seeds travel

quiz.q: Why is it good for flowers when butterflies visit them?
options: Butterflies carry pollen, which helps flowers make seeds
quiz.explain: Like bees, butterflies carry pollen from flower to flower.
quiz.mistake: Thinks butterflies only take from flowers

quiz.q: Plants and animals helping each other is like a ___.
quiz.explain: Plants give food and shelter; animals help spread pollen and seeds. Both gain.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that the help goes both ways

quiz.q: Which of these is an animal helping a plant?
options: A bird sitting in a tree's shade
A bee visiting a mustard flower
quiz.explain: The bee carries pollen and helps the mustard flower make seeds. In the others, the plant helps the animal.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up who is helping whom

teach.ask: Gappu thinks only trees help birds. He asks: do animals ever help plants?
teach.praise: Tweet! So when I drop seeds, I am planting new trees!
teach.nudge: How do bees and butterflies help flowers?

learn.hook: A fish cannot live in a desert, and a camel cannot live in the sea. Why? Every living thing has its own home!
points: A habitat is the natural home of a plant or animal, where it finds food, water and shelter.
Some habitats are on land, like forests, deserts and mountains. Others are in water, like ponds, rivers and the sea.
Camels live in deserts. Their wide, padded feet help them walk on sand, and they can go many days without water.
Yaks live in cold mountains like Ladakh. Their thick, long hair keeps them warm.
Fish breathe in water using gills. The cactus stores water in its thick stem to live in the desert. The lotus grows in ponds.

example.q: Why does a camel not sink into the desert sand like we do?
steps: Think about the camel's feet.
They are wide and padded, so its weight spreads out.
This stops its feet from sinking deep into soft sand.
example.answer: Its wide, padded feet help it walk on soft sand without sinking

learn.reallife: On a trip, look at the plants and animals around you. A beach, a hill station and a desert all have different living things!

quiz.q: What is a habitat?
options: The natural home of a plant or animal
quiz.explain: A habitat is where a living thing lives and finds food, water and shelter.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word habitat

quiz.q: Which animal is best suited to life in the desert?
quiz.explain: Camels can walk on hot sand and go many days without drinking water.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up desert animals with others

quiz.q: What is inside a camel's hump?
quiz.explain: A camel's hump stores fat, which the body can use for energy when food is scarce.
quiz.mistake: Believes the common myth that the hump stores water

quiz.q: How does a fish breathe in water?
quiz.explain: Fish have gills that take in the air dissolved in water.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fish breathe like people

quiz.q: Which animal lives in the cold mountains of Ladakh and has thick, long hair?
quiz.explain: The yak's thick, long hair keeps it warm in the freezing cold.
quiz.mistake: Does not link thick hair with cold places

quiz.q: Why does a cactus have a thick, fleshy stem?
options: To store water in the dry desert
quiz.explain: Deserts get very little rain, so the cactus stores water in its stem.
quiz.mistake: Does not link plant features to habitat

quiz.q: A frog can live both in water and on land. Which of these is also true for a frog?
options: It lives only in the desert
quiz.explain: Frogs lay their eggs in water, and the tadpoles grow there before living on land too.
quiz.mistake: Thinks frogs live only on land

quiz.q: Which plant grows in ponds?
quiz.explain: The lotus grows in ponds, with its leaves and flowers floating above the water.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up water plants and land plants

teach.ask: Gappu wants to invite a fish to live in his tree nest. He asks: is that a good idea? What is a habitat?
teach.praise: Chirp! The fish needs water, and I need my tree. We each have our own habitat!
teach.nudge: What does an animal find in its habitat?

learn.hook: A tiny ant, a street dog, a big banyan tree — they all share the Earth with us!
points: All living beings — people, animals and plants — need food, water and a safe place to live.
We should never hurt, tease or throw stones at animals.
In summer, we can keep a bowl of water out for birds and street animals.
We should not break branches or pluck flowers and leaves for no reason.
Every creature has a job in nature. Even spiders and earthworms are helpful.

example.q: Some boys are throwing stones at a street puppy. What should Priya do?
steps: Think: the puppy can get hurt and feel scared, just like us.
Priya should not join in, and should ask the boys to stop.
She should tell a trusted adult, who can help the puppy.
example.answer: Ask them to stop and tell a trusted adult

learn.reallife: Many children in India keep clay bowls of water on balconies in summer for sparrows, pigeons and mynas.

games.title: Kind or unkind to living beings?
items: Keeping water out for birds in summer
Feeding a hungry street dog with an adult

quiz.q: It is a very hot day. What can you do for the birds?
options: Keep a bowl of clean water on the balcony
quiz.explain: In hot weather, birds find it hard to get water. A bowl of water helps them.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about animals' needs

quiz.q: Your friend is pulling a cat's tail. What should you say?
options: Please stop, it hurts the cat
quiz.explain: Animals feel pain. We should be gentle with them.
quiz.mistake: Thinks animals do not feel pain

quiz.q: Why should we not pluck flowers for no reason?
options: Flowers grow back in one minute
Flowers are part of the plant and become fruits and seeds
quiz.explain: Flowers help plants make fruits and seeds. They also feed bees and butterflies.
quiz.mistake: Thinks flowers are only for decoration

quiz.q: Which is India's national bird?
quiz.explain: The peacock (Indian peafowl) is India's national bird.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a common bird

quiz.q: Which is India's national animal?
quiz.explain: The tiger is India's national animal. The elephant is the national heritage animal.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the national animal and heritage animal

quiz.q: Which is India's national tree?
quiz.explain: The banyan is India's national tree. Its branches grow roots that hang down to the ground.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a common or useful tree

quiz.q: A spider has made a web in a corner of the garden. Is the spider useful?
options: Yes, it catches flies and mosquitoes
quiz.explain: Spiders catch insects like flies and mosquitoes in their webs.
quiz.mistake: Thinks small creatures are useless

quiz.q: You see an injured bird on the road. What is the best thing to do?
options: Take it to school in your bag
Tell an adult, who can contact an animal helper or vet
quiz.explain: An adult can safely help the bird and call someone who treats animals.
quiz.mistake: Tries to handle an injured animal alone

teach.ask: Gappu sees a boy chasing a puppy. He asks: why should we be kind to animals and plants?
teach.praise: Tweet! Every living being deserves kindness, just like me!
teach.nudge: Do animals feel pain and fear like us?

learn.hook: Trees, rivers, birds and bees keep the Earth beautiful. How can we keep nature safe?
points: Nature gives us air, water, food, wood and medicines.
We protect nature by planting trees, not wasting water and not littering.
In the Chipko movement in the hills of Uttarakhand, villagers hugged trees to stop them from being cut.
The Bishnoi people of Rajasthan are known for protecting khejri trees and blackbucks.
World Environment Day is on 5 June. Van Mahotsav, a tree-planting festival, is held in the first week of July.

example.q: Why did the villagers in the Chipko movement hug the trees?
steps: The trees were going to be cut down.
The villagers needed the forest for wood, food, water and fodder.
By hugging the trees, they stopped the axes and saved the forest.
example.answer: To stop the trees from being cut and to save their forest

learn.reallife: Plant a sapling with your family and give it a name. Water it and watch it grow with you!

games.title: Protecting nature
items: Trees give shade, fruits, homes for birds and clean air.
Throwing plastic into a river is harmless.
Plastic dirties rivers and harms fish and other animals.
In the Chipko movement, people hugged trees to save them.
World Environment Day is on 5 June.
It is celebrated across the world on 5 June.
Cutting all the trees in a forest is good for the animals there.
Animals lose their food and homes when forests are cut.
Switching off fans and lights when we leave a room helps the Earth.
Saving electricity means less fuel is burnt to make it.

items.text: Villagers hugged trees in the ___ movement.
The Bishnoi people protect the ___ tree.
World Environment Day is on 5 ___.
Van Mahotsav is a festival of planting ___.

quiz.q: Which of these helps protect nature?
quiz.explain: Planting saplings adds trees that give shade, fruits and homes for birds.
quiz.mistake: Confuses harmful acts with helpful ones

quiz.q: What did people do in the Chipko movement?
options: Hugged trees to save them from being cut
quiz.explain: Villagers in the Uttarakhand hills held on to trees so they could not be cut.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what Chipko means

quiz.q: The Bishnoi people of Rajasthan are known for protecting which animal?
quiz.explain: Bishnoi communities protect blackbucks and khejri trees in the desert.
quiz.mistake: Guesses an animal not found in India

quiz.q: On which date is World Environment Day celebrated?
quiz.explain: World Environment Day is on 5 June every year.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with other special days

quiz.q: Why are forests important for animals?
options: They give animals food and homes
They have no use for animals
quiz.explain: Forests are habitats where animals find food, water and shelter.
quiz.mistake: Does not link forests with animal habitats

quiz.q: Which habit helps keep a river clean?
options: Washing plastic bags in it and leaving them there
quiz.explain: Garbage, paint and plastic make river water dirty and harm fish and other living things.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rivers can carry away any waste

quiz.q: Van Mahotsav is held in the first week of which month?
quiz.explain: Van Mahotsav, a week of planting trees, is held in the first week of July, when the rains begin in much of India.

learn.hook: Where does the water in your tap come from? Let's follow it back to where it started!
points: Rain is the main source of fresh water. Rainwater fills rivers, lakes, ponds and wells.
Some rainwater soaks into the ground. We draw this groundwater using wells, hand pumps and borewells.
Snow on high mountains melts and flows into rivers. The Ganga starts from the Gangotri glacier in the Himalayas.
Sea water is salty, so we cannot drink it or use it to water crops.
Long ago, people built stepwells (baoris or vavs) to store water, like the Rani ki Vav in Gujarat and Chand Baori in Rajasthan.

example.q: There is plenty of water in the sea. Why can't the people of Chennai simply drink sea water?
steps: Sea water tastes very salty.
Salty water is not safe for drinking.
So fresh water from rain, rivers, lakes and the ground is needed for drinking.
example.answer: Sea water is too salty to drink

points: Most of Earth's water is salty sea water. Fresh water is limited, so we must not waste it.

Use a bucket and mug for bathing instead of letting water run.

Rainwater harvesting means collecting and storing rainwater for later use.

learn.hook: Roti, dal, rice, sabzi, curd... Where does all this food come from?
points: We get food from plants and from animals.
From plants we get cereals (rice, wheat), millets (ragi, jowar, bajra), pulses (dal), fruits, vegetables and oils.
From animals we get milk, curd, paneer, eggs, honey, fish and meat.
Some families eat only plant foods and milk. Others also eat eggs, fish or meat. All these are choices families make.
Millets are healthy grains grown in India. The year 2023 was celebrated as the International Year of Millets.

example.q: Paneer is white and soft. Does it come from a plant or an animal?
steps: Paneer is made by curdling milk.
Milk comes from animals like cows and buffaloes.
So paneer is a food we get from animals.
example.answer: From an animal (it is made from milk)

learn.hook: A potato can be boiled, fried, roasted or baked. One food, so many tastes!
points: Some foods are eaten raw, like fruits, cucumbers and carrots in a salad.
Boiling: cooking in hot bubbling water, like rice, dal and eggs.
Frying: cooking in hot oil, like puris, pakoras and samosas.
Steaming: cooking with steam from boiling water, like idlis, dhoklas and modaks.
Roasting cooks food over a flame, like bhutta, and baking cooks food in an oven, like bread and cake. Cooking is always done by or with an adult!

The hot steam rising from the water cooks the idlis. This is steaming.
example.answer: By steaming

learn.hook: Travel across India on a plate! Every state has its own yummy dishes.
points: People in different parts of India eat different foods, based on what grows there and their customs.

Punjab: makki di roti with sarson da saag. Gujarat: dhokla. Rajasthan: dal baati churma. Bihar: litti chokha.
Tamil Nadu: idli and dosa. Kerala: puttu and appam. Maharashtra: puran poli and vada pav.
People living near the sea, like in Goa and Kerala, often eat fish and use coconut in cooking.

learn.hook: Germs are too tiny to see, but they can make us sick. Let's beat them with clean habits!

Wash your hands with soap and water before eating and after using the toilet. Rub for about 20 seconds.
Brush your teeth twice a day — in the morning and before going to bed.
Bathe every day, wear clean clothes and keep your nails short and clean.
Cover your mouth and nose with a tissue or your elbow when you cough or sneeze.

example.q: Kavya played in the mud and now wants to eat a banana. Her hands look only a little dirty. What should she do first?

learn.hook: Look around you. Which things did nature make, and which did people make?
points: Natural things are found in nature. People do not make them — like the sun, air, water, soil, stones and trees.
Human-made things are made by people — like chairs, pencils, buckets, bicycles and clothes.
Human-made things are made from natural things. Paper is made from wood, glass from sand, and cotton cloth from the cotton plant.
Wool comes from sheep, and silk comes from silkworms.
A tree is natural, but a wooden chair made from it is human-made.

learn.hook: A spoon can be steel, plastic or wood. What things are made of is called their material!
points: The stuff a thing is made of is its material. Wood, metal, plastic, glass, clay, paper, cloth and rubber are materials.
One thing can be made of different materials: a cup can be made of steel, glass, clay or plastic.
Many things use more than one material: a pencil has wood and graphite, and a pan has metal and a plastic handle.
We choose a material that suits the job: steel for spoons, rubber for tyres, glass for windows.
Metals like iron, steel, copper and aluminium are hard and often shiny.

example.q: Why are cooking pans made of metal but their handles made of plastic or wood?

Plastic and wood do not let heat pass through easily.
So the handle stays cool enough to hold.

Some materials soak up water, like a towel or a sponge. Others keep water out, like a plastic raincoat or a rubber boot.
Rubber bands stretch and go back. Glass and clay pots can break easily if dropped.
In water, things like a cork or a dry leaf float, while a coin or a pebble sinks.

learn.hook: Who made your clay diya, your wooden stool and your cotton kurta? Skilled hands called artisans!
points: Artisans are skilled people who make things with their hands and simple tools.
A potter shapes clay on a spinning wheel called a chaak to make pots, diyas and matkas.
A weaver makes cloth on a loom. A carpenter makes furniture from wood.
A blacksmith heats iron till it glows and beats it into tools. A basket maker weaves baskets from bamboo or cane.
Artisans often learn their skills from elders in the family, and they take great care over each piece.

example.q: A potter has wet clay. Why does he dry the pot in the sun and then bake it in a hot kiln?
steps: Wet clay is soft, so the pot can lose its shape or break.
Drying in the sun removes water from the clay.
Baking it in a kiln makes the pot hard and strong so it can hold water.

Blue pottery comes from Jaipur in Rajasthan. Bandhani, a tie-and-dye cloth, is made in Gujarat and Rajasthan.
Channapatna in Karnataka is famous for colourful wooden toys. Kondapalli in Andhra Pradesh makes wooden toys too.
Pashmina shawls come from Kashmir. Bamboo and cane crafts are famous in Assam and other states of the North-East.

learn.hook: Banana peels, chips packets, old newspapers... Is all garbage the same? No way!
points: Waste is anything we throw away because we do not need it any more.
Wet waste comes from plants and food, like peels, leftover food, tea leaves and fallen leaves. It rots and mixes with the soil.
Dry waste includes paper, plastic, glass, metal and old cloth. Most of it does not rot quickly.
Plastic does not rot. It can stay in the soil and water for a very, very long time.
Some waste, like old batteries, medicines and broken bulbs, is harmful and must be handed over carefully by an adult.

example.q: A banana peel and a plastic wrapper are left in the garden for many weeks. What happens to each?
steps: The banana peel comes from a plant. Tiny living things break it down.
It slowly rots and mixes with the soil.
The plastic wrapper does not rot. It stays almost the same for years.

learn.hook: Two bins can save the Earth a lot of trouble! Let's learn to sort our waste.

Sorted wet waste can be turned into compost, a rich manure for plants.
To make compost, put wet waste in a pit or a pot, cover it with soil or dry leaves, and wait some weeks.
Earthworms and tiny living things break the waste down into compost.

example.q: Why is it a good idea to keep wet and dry waste in separate bins?

example.answer: So wet waste can become compost and dry waste can be recycled

learn.hook: Three magic words can shrink a mountain of garbage: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle!
points: Reduce means using fewer things so less waste is made, like carrying a cloth bag instead of taking plastic bags.
Reuse means using things again, like using a jam jar to store buttons.
Recycle means turning old things into new things. Old paper becomes new paper; old glass becomes new glass.
The kabadiwala buys old newspapers, bottles and metal and sends them for recycling.
Carry a steel water bottle and a tiffin box, and say no to single-use plastic.

quiz.mistake: Mixes up recycling with composting

quiz.q: A family used to bring home 10 plastic bags a week. Now they bring only 4. By how many bags have they reduced their waste?
quiz.explain: 10 − 4 = 6 fewer plastic bags each week.
steps: Before: 10 bags
Now: 4 bags
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the difference
